Effective Pet Stain and Odor Removal Techniques In Bowie, MD

August 03, 2022
Table of Contents

We all love our furry friends, but at some.time we have to deal with pet odor and stain removal. It may not be the most fun part of having a loving pet, but figuring out how to do pet odor and stain removal in Bowie, MDwill make your life with animals even better.

If DIY pet odor and stain removalseems like too much for you to handle, you could find a pet stain and odor removal service.Shiny Carpet Cleaning is known as the bestpet stain and odor removal service in Bowie, MD, and we can take care of all of your needs.

In case you still want to tackle pet odor and stain removal in Bowie, our experts will share their best tips in this blog post. This article goes beyond telling you to buy pet stain and odor removal products, it tells you the techniques that actually work and make your home look and smell better.

Act Fast Because Time Is Of The Essence

The quicker you start working on pet stains, the more likely you are to eliminate them. As soon as you notice that your pet has made a mess, you must get to work with the cleaning techniques we outline in this article.

When a pet stain has time to set it, it goes deeper and deeper into your home, and gets harder to remove. We always want our work to be easier, and getting to a pet stain quickly makes the job much easier.

It is still possible to remove pet stains and odors after a long time, but the task is more difficult. Save yourself some energy by being vigilant and ready to clean up if there is an accident.

What Cleaners Work For Pet Stain And Odor Removal?

Many household products that you already have in your cupboard work well for pet stain and odor remover. Some items that could be helpful for this task are:

  • Baking soda
  • Vinegar
  • Dish soap
  • Salt

These items all work wonders on a fresh pet stain to pick up odors and remove spots. The items listed above are your first line of defense when your animal makes a mess in the house.

There are also specialty products, like enzyme cleaners, that breakdown the odor causing compounds in pet urine and feces. Specialty products are best when a pet stain has time to soak into your home and won’t come out with simpler methods.

Blot Up Stains, Don’t Rub Them

If you notice your pet has gone to the bathroom indoors, try to blot up as much of it as you can. Hopefully, all of the mess will come up easily and your job will be mostly done.

For urine, use a good absorbant rag or sponge and pick up as much liquid as possible. Next, add some water to dilute the stain, followed by another round of blotting.

Never rub your pets mess into the floor, because that could just make the stain soak in deeper. Just remember the old saying “rubbing is wrong, and blotting brings up the best.”

Apply A Drying Compound And Vacuum

Drying compounds are baking soda or salt. These items will absorb any liquid and odors from your pets mess and help you pick it up with your vacuum.

Sprinkle on a generous portion of your drying compound to absorb all of the liquid so that you can pick it up. Wait about ten minutes to make sure that everything gets encapsulated in the drying compound.

Use the appropriate vacuum attachment to suck up the pet stain and odors. You might want to avoid the carpet beater brush initially, because it could break up your clumps of drying compound.

Vinegar Is Good For Soaking A Stain

If the stain had a moment to soak into your carpet or flooring, soaking it with some vinegar is a good option. White vinegar is the cheapest option, but any vinegar could work in a pinch.

You can dilute the vinegar up to 50 percent if you like, but full strength is fine on anything but the most delicate surfaces. The acid in the vinegar breaks down organic compounds so they don’t end up stinking.

You can let vinegar soak in for about an hour and then you want to blot it up with a towel. You could also use a drying compound and then vacuum the whole mess up like in the last step.

Dish Soap Is Great For Greasy Stains

If your pet goes poop in the wrong place, it can leave a greasy stain. Dish soap is famous for getting rid of grease, and that makes it a great option if you are dealing with this unfortunate situation.

Just mix some dish soap and some warm water together and apply it to the stain. You can use a spray bottle, or gently wipe the soapy mixture into the stained area with a rag.

Let it sit a minute or two, then blot up the soap and water with a dry rag. Next, apply some more plain water to wash all of the soap away and hopefully your greasy stain is gone.

Using Enzyme Cleaners For Pet Stain and Odor Removal

There are several products available that use natural enzymes to break down pet stains. They are mostly effective and worth a shot if you don’t want to use other methods. They have different prices so you want to do some shopping and see which one you can afford.

Be sure to wear gloves and follow all of the manufacturer’s instructions. These products work in different ways and you may want to make sure they are safe to use on the surface that is stained.

Sometimes if one enzyme cleaner doesn’t work, another one could if it had a different formula. You may need to try several before you find the best one for your home.
